note: SKILL IMPROVEMENT: rubric design needs a 'manually-correct compaction should score ≥0.8' calibration step. My decision_retention rubric was too narrow (only verb forms). Caught only when iter 1 produced clearly-good responses scoring 0.0 on that sub-score. Suggests Phase 0 should include a small manual sanity-check: feed the rubric a hand-crafted 'good' response and confirm it scores in the 0.7-1.0 band before training.

OBSERVATION: with 95% skip rate on free-form prompts too (was hoping it was structured-list-specific), the unfixed trainer reliably reaches +3-4% composite via length compression as the dominant lift vector. The actual capability target (entity_recall) doesn't move. Suggests OPD's CURRENT effective behavior in kiln is closer to 'aggressive distillation of style' than 'targeted distillation of capability'.

KILN FINDING: rollout max_tokens has outsize effect on WHICH sub-score OPD uplifts. At 128 tok, the loss landscape's lowest-cost reduction is 'be more confident in your existing length' → length compression. At 256 tok, OPD has room to favor content tokens (entities/identifiers). Implication: max_tokens should be set wider than the natural response length so the gradient has room to land on capability, not on format. Could automate: detect avg response length in baseline, set rollout max_tokens to 1.5-2x that.

SKILL IMPROVEMENT (next session): Phase 0 should include a 'rollout sizing' check. Run baseline at the proposed max_tokens to see if it's already saturating the format constraint. If yes, the OPD signal will be confounded by format-compression dynamics. Either widen max_tokens or accept the confound.
